chunks: He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad reported to me from his father Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid al-Qummi, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id al-Ahwazi, from al-Nadhr ibn Suwayd and Ibn Abi Najran together, from Asim, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, may Allah's blessings be upon them both, that Abu Dharr, may Allah have mercy on him, used to say:
O Seeker of knowledge! It is as though nothing in this world was of any worth, except a deed whose good benefits and whose evil harms, except for those upon whom Allah has mercy.

O Seeker of knowledge! Do not let family or wealth distract you from yourself. On the day you part from them, you will be like a guest who spent a night among them and then departed in the morning to others. This world and the next are like a station at which you halted and then moved on to another. The span between death and resurrection is but like a sleep from which you slept and then awoke.
O Seeker of knowledge! Send ahead for your standing before Allah, for you are mortgaged against your deeds, and as you judge so shall you be judged.

O Seeker of knowledge! Pray before a time comes when you can find neither night nor day in which to pray! The example of prayer for its performer, with Allah's permission, is like a man who entered upon a king, and the king listened to him attentively until he finished his need. Likewise, the Muslim—as long as he is in his prayer, Allah continues to look upon him until he finishes his prayer.

O Seeker of knowledge! Give charity before a time comes when you can neither give anything nor withhold it! The example of charity for its giver is like a man who was wanted by a people for blood, and he said: Do not kill me, and grant me a term so that I may strive to please you. Likewise, the Muslim, with Allah's permission—every time he gives in charity, a knot around his neck is untied, until Allah takes people while being pleased with them, and whoever Allah is pleased with is freed from the Fire.
O Seeker of knowledge! A heart that has no truth in it is like a ruined house that has no one to restore it.
O Seeker of knowledge! This tongue is a key to good and a key to evil, so seal your mouth as you seal your gold and your silver.
O Seeker of knowledge! These are parables that Allah has set forth for people, and none comprehend them except the knowledgeable.

key_terms.عتق من النار: Freed from the Fire—release from Hellfire as a consequence of divine pleasure
key_terms.كما تدين تدان: As you judge, so shall you be judged—a proverbial expression about reciprocal justice
key_terms.مبتغي العلم: Seeker of knowledge—Abu Dharr's repeated form of address, reflecting the Islamic emphasis on learning
key_terms.مرتهن: Mortgaged/pledged—a person whose deeds are held as collateral for their standing in the Hereafter

ai.seo_question: What are Abu Dharr al-Ghifari's famous exhortations to seekers of knowledge?
ai.summary: Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, the renowned companion of the Prophet known for his asceticism and fierce devotion to truth, delivers a series of exhortations to seekers of knowledge. Transmitted through Imam al-Baqir (AS), these counsels address the fleeting nature of worldly life, the urgency of prayer and charity before death, the metaphor of the tongue as a key to good and evil, and the parable of a heart devoid of truth as a ruined house. Abu Dharr was exiled to al-Rabadha for his outspoken criticism of wealth accumulation, and his words reflect the deep ascetic tradition valued in early Shi'i thought.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him
